### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via resolvePredicateRelated (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `18fe10eeca2bb522520ca3cbc057d78fad81041d` — the merge of head `6586f417fb3e86495afc657428ba703071d9e226` into base `51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 18fe10eeca2bb522520ca3cbc057d78fad81041d && git checkout 18fe10eeca2bb522520ca3cbc057d78fad81041d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 6586f417fb3e86495afc657428ba703071d9e226 && git checkout -B drift-repro 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 && git merge --no-ff 6586f417fb3e86495afc657428ba703071d9e226

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6586f417fb3e86495afc657428ba703071d9e226`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22892 (body and all four comments: triage entry check 6113638846, ruling 6115662038 which binds, claim 6116757077, os-dev-report 6118217501); card #22519's ruling 6107211425 and PR #22891's contract record 6113514249 as the precedent this card extends; PR #22956 (body, its one comment — the docs-drift advisory — its file list, and the net diff of `origin/main...` the head: 4 files, +478 / −23, fetched into a review ref and read as objects, plus the two-dot diff against current `main` for the merge); the head's check-runs; and on `origin/main` only `resolvePredicateRelated`, `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` and their call sites in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `RelatedFieldBinding` / `RelatedUnavailableReason` / `traversalRefusal` in `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`, row 29b of `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, and ADR-0055 §3. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Disclosure rule kept: classes, positions and functions only.

**Check-runs at the final read:** 34 runs, no `failure`: 26 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 6 still `in_progress` — the six `Test Core` shards. Of the seven required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success`; `Test Core` is not yet concluded on any shard. `Check Changeset` is `success`, and so are the four `Type Check ·` jobs behind the aggregate. Every `check:*` gate — `check:system-context-census`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:durability-log-level` among them — is therefore concluded green by `Lint & Repo Gates` on this head. The test families the pending shards carry (the new pin file, #22891's pins, the #18682 suite and plugin-security's real-rules suites among them) are concluded by those six runs, not by this record: the owning seat arms nothing until every shard reads `success`, and a red among them re-opens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change the diff implies — one narrowing, for non-system callers, on a predicate rule's one-hop read through a `master_detail` FK only.** Read on the head, `engine.ts` `resolvePredicateRelated` (`:9220`): after the existing own-read branch for a related object no organization wall scopes, a new `else if` (`:9358`) keys on the function's existing `bound` (`:9262`, "not SYSTEM") and on the traversed field's `type === 'master_detail'` — the same arbiter the reference check uses to pick `masterDetailHeaderExists` (main `:8661`). It calls `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` (`:9366`) with the deduplicated id set under the caller's own context, and the elevated, tenant-kept read then runs over `readSet` (`:9370`), the door's answer, instead of the asked ids. A header the door does not return never enters `byId` and the entry carries no `ownRead`, so the per-row binding (`:9415`) is `unresolved` — the same reason, and therefore the same `traversalRefusal` sentence ("the related record was not found", `_record` `rule_violation` inside `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`), that a header existing nowhere already got on this path. Where it bites: a write that landed on `main` — an update by id or a bulk update of a detail whose stored FK names an unreadable header in a state the rule accepts, with no reference value re-supplied, so #22891's reference check never ran — is now refused; on insert and on a repoint the refusal's shape moves from the FK field's `reference_not_found` to the record-level rule refusal, which is the answer a nonexistent header already got there. Nothing loosens: the door's set is a subset of what the elevated read returned before. **Right** — this is the ruling's two-read shape, and it reuses PR #22891's door; the diff adds no method, so there is no second helper.

**One answer for nowhere, unreadable-open and unreadable-locked, on every door and the preview — right.** The change sits inside the one resolver every door calls: the `validate()` preview (`:14083`), insert single and array with `insertMany` as its partial form (`:15043`), update by id with the repoint (`:16649`), and the predicate/bulk update (`:16945`). None of the four call sites changes, so no door can keep the old read. Pinned in the head's new file: the three headers answer identically (envelope, field codes and message with the id removed) on insert, batch insert, update by id, repoint by id and bulk update; the preview's issue list is equal across the three; the partial `insertMany` fails the unreadable rows as it fails the nonexistent one and lands only the readable open one.

**A refused door read binds as nothing returned — right, and in the fail-closed direction.** `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` (`:8764`) catches its own failure, logs once at `warn` and returns an empty set (`:8787`), so the branch takes the `readSet.size === 0` exit (`:9367`): an empty `byId`, no `ownRead`, every header `unresolved`. The resolver's outer `catch` (which would have produced `unreadable`) is never reached by a door refusal, so a caller whose read of the header object is refused outright gets the nowhere answer and not a distinguishable one. Pinned for the refused-read caller on all five doors, readable headers included. `warn` is the right level: the failure reaches the caller as a refusal and nothing claims to persist.

**The elevated read runs only for headers the door returned — right.** `:9370` reads `$in` over `readSet`. The mechanism pin asserts, for an unreadable header, exactly one non-elevated `find` on the header object and no elevated read, and for a readable one the door read followed by the elevated read of that id alone.

**System callers unchanged — right.** `bound` is false for `isSystem`, so neither the own-read branch nor the new one runs; `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` would in any case return every asked id for a system context (`:8771`). Pinned: a system caller's insert and update are judged on the header's stored state whoever owns it, with zero non-elevated header reads.

**Plain `lookup` traversal unchanged — right.** The new branch keys on `master_detail`; a `lookup` to a walled object keeps the elevated read over `ids` (`readSet` defaults to `ids`). Pinned by the lookup-line control: the stored state is judged, locked refused and open landed, and no non-elevated read is issued. This is the ruling's scope line.

**Unwalled related objects unchanged — right.** The own-read branch runs first and is byte-identical apart from assigning `readSet`; a master-detail FK to a federated or untenanted master therefore still takes the own-read path, where every miss — stored or not — is already `unreadable`, one answer on that object, so the ruling's "unreadable equals nowhere" was already met there. The `else if` placement means the two bounds never compose, which is correct: both answer the same question.

**#22891's three seams unchanged — right.** `resolveMasterDetailParent`, `resolveMasterDetailParents` and `masterDetailHeaderExists` are outside the hunks; the diff touches the resolver's body and docblock only. The dev reports #22891's 30 pins green on both the mutated and the unmutated run; `Test Core` on the head is the merged-generation reading.

**A readable header still judged on stored values, a hidden or masked state column included — right.** The door is projected to `id` and its rows' contents are never consulted; the value read is the unchanged `isSystem: true` read. Pinned: locked refuses with the rule's own message and open lands on all five doors; a middleware that hides or masks the state column for the caller still yields the rule's verdict on the stored value.

**Docblock and row 29b — right.** The "Read under SYSTEM authority, like `parent`" section is gone; the new section separates the VALUES question (still SYSTEM, projection-bounded) from the ROWS question and states the three arms — the master-detail header through the door, an unwalled object through the own read, a plain lookup elevated alone — and the system caller's stand-down. The inline "accepted cost" comment now names the two inference channels that remain (a hidden column on a readable row, a plain lookup on a walled object) and excludes the unreadable master-detail header. Row 29b's "Get" column lists all three bounds a system caller skips, states that a non-system caller is held to all three with the one-answer rule and the stored-value rule, and states that a plain `lookup` to a walled object asks no door for any caller; each clause matches the code read above. The row's anchor is unchanged and no `isSystem` read was added, so the census does not move (dev-reported OK, and `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:system-context-census`, is `success` on the head).

**Public surface — none changed.** No `export` line in the diff; one local `readSet` binding and one branch inside a `private` method; no new method, type or option. `@objectstack/objectql` is the one published package touched; the test file and `content/docs` publish nothing.

**ADR-0055 §3 — not touched and not contradicted.** Its master-edit gate covers `controlled_by_parent` details in plugin-security; this change is a read bound inside the engine's rule evaluation and leaves that gate as it is.

**Cost, noted and not a contract matter.** One id-projected caller read per master-detail reference field a rule reads through, once per write batch, for a non-system caller — the shape #22891 already pays on the header binding.

### ② Semver level

**Changeset:** `.changeset/22892-predicate-related-master-detail.md`, `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, body headed BREAKING (an accept-set narrowing) under the launch-window convention, carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its category walk, the FROM / TO statement, the bindings list and the one-line fix (grant the writer read on the master, or declare the detail `controlled_by_parent`). **Matches what the diff publishes:** nothing is added to the accept set (`no`); the accept set narrows for non-system callers on the doors named above (`(narrowing)`, which AGENTS.md reads as BREAKING); no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape moves, so no migration prescription is owed and `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the true category. No `skip-changeset` label (labels: `documentation`, `size/l`, `tests`, `tooling`).

**The `Clause-②:` line agrees in all three places and is the true value.** PR body line 2: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Changeset: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Claim 6116757077: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. True, because the one direction the diff moves is refusing writes that landed (the stored-FK update doors) and reshaping other refusals into the nowhere answer; no write refused on `main` lands on the head. `minor` for a breaking narrowing follows the convention the changeset names and the precedent #22891's changeset set under the same ruling family; `Check Changeset` is `success`, and `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:adr-0087-registration` (dev-reported exit 0), is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

**Deviations (seven), each answered:**
1. Attribution: model-free commit trailers and the session-URL PR footer, over a harness reminder asking otherwise — **accepted; this is the rule.** The three authored commits each carry the `Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair and no model identifier; the merge commit carries none.
2. `origin/main` merged before the PR opened, the os-regen driver deferring `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` — **accepted, and verified here.** The two-dot diff of the head against current `main` differs in that file by the row 29b line only, so nothing `main` brought to the page was dropped; the dev reports the deferral marker cleared and the pre-push hook passing, which the push itself attests. `main` has moved three commits past the merge (a board-snapshot workflow, a docs-deploy workflow and the v18 releases landing page); none touches `packages/objectql`, the page or the changeset; the queue rebuilds on current `main`, and no re-merge is owed before this record.
3. The full objectql suite moved to the background and was waited on in-turn by recorded PID — **accepted**; a process matter with no file effect, and the head's `Test Core` is the authority on the merged generation.
4. Lock contention, two queue-timeouts retried, no holder stalled — **accepted**; no file effect.
5. A scratch probe file reproduced the three answers and was deleted before the first test commit — **accepted, and verified**: no commit on the branch adds it and the head's tree holds no such file.
6. File surface kept; the `rule-validator.ts` docblock gap noted, not edited — **accepted** (the finding below).
7. Worktree removed, nothing left uncommitted — **accepted**.

**Out-of-scope finding (one) — answered, not escalated.** `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` is outside the claim's surface and was not edited. Read on `main`: the `RelatedFieldBinding` docblock names the projection and the unwalled own-read as the related read's bounds; the `unresolved` arm of `RelatedUnavailableReason` reads "the related record was not found"; and — a third site the dev did not list — the `related` option's docblock on the evaluation options says the read is made "like `parent`" under SYSTEM authority. After this diff each is incomplete and none is false: a header the door withholds IS not found as far as the rule is concerned, and the `related` read is again like `parent` on the master-detail arm. Prime Directive #10's test (a reproducible defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap) is not met, so an acceptance note is the right carrier and no card is owed; the engine docblock the ruling ordered rewritten is the one that states the rule, and it does. Non-blocking.

**Governance:** no governed-surface path in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`; 501 changed lines, under the 3,000-line threshold; head repo equals base repo; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, assignee the card's; the PR is draft and unarmed, as the claim's "one contract-tier review before the queue" requires. This record is that review.

**VERDICT: PASS**
